title: [observability] the owner's interventions through the queue: lead-mac's posts in sync/queue.md counted in /api/interventions (owner_decision, steering) when the ranges file names the queue
prompt:
Spawn, objective 156 [observability] (after 148): the owner's interventions through the queue count. `/api/interventions`, and so the Home card's figure and Core lines' `observability.interventions_per_agent_hour`, add lead-mac's posts in sync/queue.md as the owner's interventions: `owner_decision` and `steering`. Only when the ranges file names the queue. Core line 3; sync/proposal-156-interventions-rev-b.md, scoped with projects-47 on 2026-11-14 (156a there; 156b, reviewer spans, is 157).

Where things stand (148's throwaway: ffda22f5 + 141's diff f52f6993 + 148's diff 1b9d0e8c, the tree 148 was reviewed on):
- The figure is `/api/interventions?window=24h`'s `per_agent_hour` (crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/interventions.rs over the store's `interventions_window`). Its numerator is what the owner did through Spawn: commands (one per intent), mission resumes, owner tasks, cancel-and-reassign, pauses.
- On 11-14 it read 0.0 over 78.5 agent-hours. The same day the queue held 46 `## lead-mac HH:MM — …` headings (26 the owner's decisions, 20 lead-mac's steering): nearly everything the owner did went through the queue.
- qpost (sync/tools/qpost) writes each heading as `## <who> HH:MM — <text>`, stamped by this host's local clock (+08:00). There is no date in a heading.

Read: crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/interventions.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines.rs (`ranges_path`, `read_ranges`, the interventions part of the reading), docs/storage.md (the ranges file), sync/tools/qpost.

Required behaviour.
- The setting, in the ranges file (`SPAWN_CORE_LINES_FILE`, by default `<workspace root>/core-lines.json`): `{"observability": {"queue_file": "<absolute path>", "queue_utc_offset_minutes": <minutes east of UTC>}}`. The offset defaults to 0, and to 0 when beyond 14 h. A relative path, no `queue_file`, or no ranges file: nothing is read, and the answer is exactly as before (by_kind holds only the kinds it holds today).
- New crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/queue_posts.rs reads the file:
  - a heading is a line `## <who> <H:MM or HH:MM> <text>`, the text with its leading dash (— or -) and spaces trimmed. Any other line is no heading.
  - Only `who` = `lead-mac` counts. The lead's headings never count ("Owner decision:", "owner gate PENDING" and "Owner question" included: the lead relays what lead-mac already posted), nor a reviewer's.
  - kind `owner_decision` when the text holds the word "owner" in any case (split on non-alphanumerics: "ownership" is not the word), else `steering`.
  - The day: read back from the end of the file. The newest heading is on the local date of now, or the day before when its time is more than 5 minutes later than now's local time. Each earlier heading whose time is more than 12 h later than the heading after it is a day before it (the nearer of the two readings); otherwise the same day, so a heading stamped minutes earlier than the one above it is not a midnight. Local time is UTC plus the offset.
  - Why 12 h (R1, rev-f F1): the live queue.md has headings out of order by 15 and 28 minutes (line 1171 lead-mac 01:00, then line 1178 lead 00:32; line 2233 lead-mac 23:55, then line 2259 lead-mac 23:40). R0's 5-minute rule took each for a midnight and dated every older post a day early: line 1842, lead-mac 17:05 on 11-12 by its screenshot, came out 11-11. Over the live file the 12 h rule finds exactly its 4 real midnights (the 5-minute rule finds 7); the largest gap between consecutive headings is 10.4 h. More than 24 h with no post still breaks the reading; that is the dated qpost's to fix (below).
  - A heading with no time (`## lead-mac — …`; 17 on live, all old) is no heading and is not counted.
  - An item per post in the window `[since, until)`, in the store's items' shape: `{kind, at_ms, principal: "lead-mac", agent: null, session: null, line, commands: [], attempts: null, outcome: null, source: "queue"}`. The line is the text with control characters dropped, cut at 120 characters with "…" after.
  - The file is read whole up to 4 MiB, beyond that its last 4 MiB from the first whole line. The text is kept in memory and read again only when the file's length or modification time changes.
- interventions.rs `measure` appends the posts to the store's items, sorts all items newest first (stable: the store's order on ties), and counts them in `total`, `by_kind` and `per_agent_hour`. When the queue is named, `by_kind` holds `owner_decision` and `steering`, at 0 when none fell in the window. The placing uses the wall clock (`verify::now_ms`), the window the request's.
- serve/core_lines.rs gains `queue_settings()`: the ranges file's text through `queue_posts::settings`.
- docs/storage.md, after the ranges file's paragraph: the setting, what counts, the day rule, the read and its cap, and that the Fleet strip and the scorecard do not count the posts yet (158).
- Nothing else changes: the store, its reads, the other kinds, /api/fleet, the scorecard, the web card (it shows a row's kind as written, so "owner_decision" and "steering" show without a change).
- Polled read: no store read is added or changed. The added cost per answer is one read of the ranges file (Core lines already reads it per request), a stat of the queue file, and a line scan of the kept text (952 KB on live today). The file is read only when it changed.

Not changed, and why (the lead's decision of 11-14): `/api/fleet`'s `health.human_per_agent_hour` and the scorecard's autonomy are computed in SQL in crates/spawn-postgres. They do not count the queue posts. Bringing them to the same count is follow-up 158 [observability], after 156: one key, `interventions_24h`, added to fleet_health's existing answer, with serve.rs adding the posts, and the scorecard's autonomy the same, with a 103-style check. So that no two numbers stand under one name meanwhile, the live core-lines.json names no `queue_file` until 158 lands. The lead sets it then, by hand, and Home, the guardrail, the Fleet strip and the scorecard move together.

Follow-up, for the lead (asked: list every reader of the `## <who> HH:MM —` form before a date is added to it): a dated heading (`## <who> YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM — …`) from qpost is its own small change later. The readers of the form today, on this host:
- sync/tools/qpost writes it, and reads nothing.
- sync/tools/branch-status appends one plain line to queue.md (`--post`) and parses no heading; tools/test-branch-status.sh checks that line count in a scratch queue.
- sync/bb-http/run.sh names queue.md only in a comment (its quiet-host wait reads owner-gate.state).
- sync/tools/tp/*.py and store-first-copy mention the queue in comments only.
- Spawn: no reader before 156. With 156, queue_posts.rs is the only parser. Its rule takes `H:MM`/`HH:MM` right after the author. A dated heading (`## lead-mac 2026-11-14 07:10 — …`) would not parse as a heading and would not count, so the dated qpost must come with a queue_posts change that takes the date when present (and the wrap rule only for older headings).
- The Mac's tools that read queue.md are lead-mac's to list.

Unit tests (crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/queue_posts.rs):
- `lead_macs_posts_are_placed_by_the_midnight_wraps_and_counted_by_kind` (R1: same name, its sequence rewritten): a queue 8 h east of UTC with two real midnights (23:56 above 00:34; the lead's 23:50 above 00:20), rev-f's live backsteps on the same day (01:00 then the lead's 00:32: 28 minutes; 23:55 then 23:40: 15 minutes), 00:18 under 00:20, a lead heading and a reviewer's not counted, a list line and a heading with no time not headings. Then the day's window holds 5; the 12 h line (12:59 above 01:00 the same day, 13:01 above 01:00 a day back); a hostile heading (an escape character, HTML, 200 more characters) keeps its text without the escape character, cut at 120 then "…"; a newest heading more than 5 minutes later than now is yesterday's, 3 minutes later today's; offset 0 is UTC; "ownership" is steering and "Owner:" an owner decision.
- `the_queue_is_read_only_when_the_ranges_file_names_it`: the settings (an absolute path and its offset; 0 beyond 14 h; nothing for no queue_file, a relative path, a broken file, no file).
- `the_file_is_read_from_its_tail_and_again_when_it_changes`: a file over 4 MiB gives its tail from the first whole line; a changed file is read again.
And interventions.rs `the_answer_counts_one_per_intent_and_says_the_retries` (updated, not renamed): an owner_decision item counts in `total`, `by_kind` and `per_agent_hour`.
Each rule removed alone fails a test or the scenario. No test is renamed or dropped.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard.rs (`mod queue_posts`), crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/queue_posts.rs (new), crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/interventions.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines.rs (`queue_settings`; 148 is in this file, 156 is written after it), docs/storage.md, rsi/scenarios/156.sh (new). One crate.
The throwaway (R1) is +810 −7 on 148's throwaway (ffda22f5 + 141 + 148); R0 is under sync/obj-156/r0/, and 156-r1-delta.diff is R1's change on R0:
- code: queue_posts.rs 232 lines with its doc comments, interventions.rs +32 −7, core_lines.rs +8, scorecard.rs +1, docs +17;
- tests: queue_posts.rs 144, interventions.rs +7;
- 156.sh +369.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/156.sh. Black box through `spawn serve` on a seeded history (one execution from 10 h to 2 h ago: 8 agent-hours in the day; a mission resumed 5 h ago) and a scratch queue file named in the ranges file with offset 480, its headings stamped by the wall clock as qpost stamps them, oldest first, at hours before now: -30 lead-mac "OWNER DECISIONS: older than the day"; -29 lead "owner gate PENDING"; -20 lead-mac "[recoverability] Leak check done"; -12 rev-b; -6 lead "Owner question: …"; -5 lead-mac "OWNER DECISIONS (by the owner): no second host"; -4 lead "Owner decision: relayed, not counted"; -3 lead-mac "F4 PASSES"; 3 h 20 min before now, below it, a lead heading stamped 20 minutes before it (as live has: the same day, not a midnight); -1 lead-mac a hostile heading (an escape character, `<b>`, `&`, "the owner", 200 more characters).
(1) /api/interventions?window=24h: total 5, per_agent_hour 0.625; by_kind owner_decision 2, steering 2, resume 1, the other Spawn kinds 0; the queue items, newest first, lead-mac's four with their kinds and lines; all items newest first.
(2) window=7d: the post 30 h ago counts too (total 6, owner_decision 3, steering 2). A day ending 2 days ago: total 0, and by_kind says the queue's kinds at 0.
(3) Core lines' observability.interventions_per_agent_hour: 0.625.
(4) The hostile heading's line: the escape character dropped, `<b>` and `&` as text, 120 characters then "…".
(5) A post appended to the file counts at the next answer (steering 3).
(6) With the ranges file naming no queue: total 1, per_agent_hour 0.125, by_kind exactly cancel_reassign, command, owner_task, resume.
On the base (148's throwaway), 156.sh exits 1 with 9 checks failed, the first "(1) the day's interventions: a resume and lead-mac's four posts over 8 agent-hours: expected [{"total":5,"per_agent_hour":0.625}], got [{"total":1,"per_agent_hour":0.125}]"; (6) passes there. R0's binary fails 7 checks of R1's 156.sh ((1), (2), (3), (5)): the lead's backstep moved the older posts a day early.
On the throwaway:
- 156.sh passes;
- the kept scenarios that read /api/interventions or the ranges file pass: 049, 100, 102, 103, 084;
- the unit tests queue_posts and interventions:: (5), cargo fmt --check and clippy -D warnings pass;
- the test list (spawn-cli + spawn-postgres) gains the three new names, and none is missing.
22 mutants, each alone (mut156.py), each from a fresh copy of R1, each built (22 distinct binaries), each run with the unit tests queue_posts and interventions:: and 156.sh:

- owner-substring ("ownership" taken for the word): the unit test;
- no-wrap (every heading on the newest's day): the unit test and (1), (2), (5);
- wrap-five-minutes (R0's rule): the unit test and (1), (2), (3), (5); wrap-an-hour, wrap-eleven-hours and wrap-thirteen-hours: the unit test (the 12 h line);
- no-slack (the newest heading's 5 minutes dropped) and newest-today (a newest heading later than now kept on today): the unit test;
- no-offset (the offset ignored): the unit test and (1), (3), (5);
- offset-unbounded and relative-file: the settings test;
